headline: Migration safaris cost more due to demand, not superior quality
summary: Migration-focused safaris typically cost $800-1,500/person/day compared to $400-800 for comparable off-peak trips. The premium reflects demand (limited camps, peak season) rather than intrinsically better experiences. Calving season (January-March) offers migration at slightly lower prices than crossing season (August). Green season visits miss some migration events but cost 30-50% less.

assumptions.text: Migration pricing reflects demand and scarcity, not superior experience quality.
Calving season is less expensive than crossing season despite excellent wildlife.
Green season and shoulder months offer 30-50% savings with trade-offs.

gains: Peak season: Highest probability of migration encounters
Premium camps: Better guides, positioning, and service
Calving season: Predator action at lower prices than crossings
Shoulder months: Migration present with reduced crowds and prices
losses: August camps: Book 12+ months ahead or pay premium
Green season: Lower migration probability, some rainfall

change_conditions: If budget is constrained, calving season offers excellent value for migration.
If flexibility exists, shoulder months (June, late October) balance cost and probability.
If budget is unlimited, August northern Serengeti/Mara maximizes crossing probability.
If willing to accept lower probability, green season delivers substantial savings.
